title: Tarriela rebuts Chinese scholar's claim that Ayungin Shoal is Chinese territory
summary: Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) spokesperson Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela on Tuesday rejected a Chinese scholar's claim that Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal is Chinese territory, stressing that the disputed…

blocks.text: Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) spokesperson Rear Admiral Jay Tristan Tarriela on Tuesday rejected a Chinese scholar's claim that Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal is Chinese territory, stressing that the disputed feature lies within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone (EEZ).

Tarriela made the remarks after Dr. Zheng Zhihua of Shanghai Jiao Tong University argued that China was justified in using water cannons against Philippine vessels in the South China Sea, claiming that Beijing was merely defending its territory.

The exchange took place during a discussion on whether the proposed Code of Conduct (COC) between China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in the South China Sea should be legally binding.

Zheng said a COC would be ineffective without a fundamental consensus among China and ASEAN member states. He cited what he described as a key disagreement, claiming that the Philippines had been occupying Second Thomas Shoal, which he called Chinese territory, for 27 years.
He also defended China's use of water cannons against Philippine fishing and coast guard vessels operating within the Philippines' EEZ.
"China only uses water cannons as a big power. I think if other countries occupy your land territory, you only use water canals to defend your territory integrity," Zheng said.
"I would just like to correct you in saying that China does not have any territorial jurisdiction whatsoever in Second Thomas Shoal," he said.

"The last time I checked, Second Thomas Shoal only has a distance of 125 nautical miles from the Philippines. And it is our exclusive economic zone, not China's," Tarriela added, citing the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), which provides for an EEZ extending up to 200 nautical miles from a country's baselines.
Zheng countered by saying: "No country occupied Second Thomas Shoal as easy like Philippines did."
Indonesian scholar Dr. Dewi Fortuna Anwar, meanwhile, said ASEAN should intervene to help defuse tensions in the South China Sea.
Anwar said China should reach out to ASEAN member states rather than assert its power, warning that displays of might would not resolve territorial disputes.
"To jeopardize the goodwills of ASEAN countries over these issues in the South China Sea, I think is, you know, you are shooting your foot," she said.

In July 2016, an arbitral tribunal under the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague ruled in favor of the Philippines in its case against China, rejecting Beijing's expansive claims over much of the South China Sea based on its nine-dash line.
The tribunal also ruled that areas of the Spratly Islands, including Mischief Reef, Second Thomas Shoal and Reed Bank, are within the Philippines' EEZ and continental shelf.

It further found that China had unlawfully prevented Filipino fishermen from accessing Scarborough Shoal, also known as Panatag Shoal, which it recognized as a traditional fishing ground for both Filipino and Chinese fishermen.
The ruling stemmed from an arbitration case initiated by the Philippines in 2013. China refused to participate in the proceedings and has rejected the ruling.— MCG, GMA News
